signals.title: AUD/CHF — G10 Bilateral Theme + Geopolitical Leader
signals.text: AUD/USD trades at 0.7167, maintaining its position above the SMA20/50/200 cluster (0.7057/0.7002/0.6954) as the top G10 performer this week. The currency is supported by a +435bp carry premium over CHF (RBA 4.35% vs SNB 0.0%) and fresh TIER-1 geopolitical headlines regarding impending Iran sanctions, which often buoy commodity-linked proxies. While AUD COT LF positioning is long at +49,749 (pctl 81), retail sentiment is 90% short, creating a significant institutional-retail divergence that often fuels further upside on retail capitulation. AUD 10Y yields at 5.03% provide a +29bp spread over US 10Y, further cementing the fundamental bid. Trade bias: Long AUD/CHF; carry advantage and geopolitical tailwinds dominate the pair's trend. Catalyst: next RBNZ meeting (mkt: 88% hike priced) 2 Sep (proxy for Oceania sentiment). Risk: ESI of -10.3 for AUD signals data is starting to miss expectations, which could eventually weigh on the RBA's hold stance.

signals.title: USD/JPY — Options Complacency + Carry-Geopolitical Conflict
signals.text: USD/JPY trades at 159.14, testing the SMA20 at 159.43 amid rising geopolitical tensions in the Strait of Hormuz. Despite the +275bp Fed-BoJ carry advantage (Fed 3.75% vs BoJ 1.0%), the options market is pricing in significant downside protection with a 25d risk reversal at -1.96. Unusually, USD/JPY IV at 7.2% sits below HV30 at 8.8%, resulting in a negative VRP of -1.6% that suggests the market is underpricing potential volatility from verbal or actual intervention near 160.00. JPY COT LF net short of -73,641 shows carry remains crowded, but the correlation with VIX has flipped to positive (+0.434), signaling JPY is currently failing to act as a safe haven during localized stress. Trade bias: Neutral USD/JPY; carry support is offset by acute intervention risk and extreme negative options skew. Catalyst: next BoJ meeting (mkt: 65% hike priced) 18 Sep. Risk: A break above 160.00 triggers immediate BoJ/MoF action, forcing an unwind of the -73k spec short position.

signals.title: GBP/USD — Elevated Volatility Premium + Speculative Overstretch
signals.text: GBP/USD trades at 1.3645, holding above its SMA20/50/200 cluster (1.3485/1.3395/1.3427) following a rally to 6.5-month highs. COT LF net long positioning is near a 52-week extreme at +46,070 (pctl 94, z +1.45), suggesting the move is becoming crowded among speculators. This positioning is met with a massive +5.1% Vol Risk Premium (IV 11.0% vs HV30 5.9%), indicating that institutional players are paying a high premium to hedge the current level rather than chasing the breakout. While the Fed-BoE carry is neutral at 0bp, the UK 10Y yield of 5.06% offers a +32bp premium over the US 10Y, providing the primary yield support for the move. Trade bias: Bearish GBP/USD; crowded speculative longs and extreme hedging costs suggest a near-term mean reversion toward 1.3500. Catalyst: Jackson Hole Symposium 27-29 Aug. Risk: Continued USD ESI misses (Index -15.3) further weaken the dollar, allowing the GBP long squeeze to delay.

signals.title: EUR/USD — Divergence between ESI and Technical Position
signals.text: EUR/USD holds at 1.1678, comfortably above its SMA200 (1.1634) and recent SMA20/50 support levels. The pair's fundamental backdrop is mixed, as ECB's Cipollone recently downplayed stagnation risks, while the EUR ESI has turned positive at +9.4, outperforming the USD ESI of -15.3. However, EUR COT LF positioning remains deeply short at -76,035 (pctl 10, z -1.99), marking a significant divergence between improving eurozone data surprises and bearish speculative sentiment. The +135bp Fed-ECB carry advantage for the USD remains the structural ceiling, but the options market shows a mild call skew (+0.47 RR), suggesting a possible short-covering rally if US data continues to miss. Trade bias: Bullish EUR/USD; technical support and data outperformance favor a squeeze of the pctl 10 spec short. Catalyst: next ECB meeting (mkt: 75% hike priced) 10 Sep. Risk: ECB pivot to a more dovish stance on stagnation fears would validate the spec short and break SMA200 support.
